definitions: Paul Adolph Volcker (1927-2019) was an American economist who served as the 12th Chair of the Federal Reserve from 1979 to 1987.

Volcker Rule: A specific provision of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act that restricts U.S. banks from making certain kinds of speculative investments that do not benefit their customers.
examples: Volcker was appointed by President Carter.
The Volcker Rule aims to prevent future financial crises.
